item.title: EDITORIAL: Wait and see on free school meals
item.description: Feeding hungry children is an undoubtedly noble cause, and one that addresses a growing societal need, but government responsibility to provide aid must be bounded by judicious limits that reflect the state’s fiduciary responsibility to all citizens. A proposal to provide meals for all students in the state’s public school system is neither sensible nor practical, particularly when other issues — many within the education apparatus — require more attention and funding.

item.title: Agricultural listening session on Saturday
item.description: HONOLULU — U.S. Rep. Jill Tokuda will host an agricultural listening session for people in the industry — including ranchers, farmers and producers — on Saturday, following the Town Hall Meeting at the Elsie Wilcox Elementary School cafeteria.

item.title: Strong showing for McRoberts in Kauai Interscholastic Federation wrestling
item.description: LIHUE — Kapaa High School girls wrestler Avah McRoberts continued to dominate the girls wrestling scene on Saturday during the Kauai Interscholastic Federation wrestling matches held at the Wilcox Gymnasium at Island School.

item.title: Steps taken to control coconut rhinoceros beetle
item.description: The Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity will move forward with starting an interim rule-making process to combat the coconut rhinoceros beetle on the Big Island.

item.title: UH report: Limited income growth slows Hawaii economy
item.description: When adjusted for decades of suppressed wages — and paired with the “sky-high cost of living” — Hawaii’s economy actually ranks near the bottom nationally, along with parts of Appalachia, the rural South and the Mississippi Delta, according to a new report released today by the University of Hawaii Economic Research Organization.

item.title: Workshops on Mauna Kea management head to Hawaii Island
item.description: LIHUE — The Mauna Kea Stewardship and Oversight Authority (MKSOA), in partnership with Kua o Wakea, completed its fifth statewide community workshop Tuesday evening at Kauai Community College, marking the midpoint of a series of public engagement sessions focused on shaping the future management of Mauna Kea.

item.title: Hawaii lawmakers consider allowing residents to kill feral chickens
item.description: Hawaii residents could be allowed to kill feral chickens in their community in the latest effort to help resolve a perennial issue that continues to divide neighbors who both hate and love them.

item.title: Plenty of work for Legislature
item.description: Hawaii’s watersheds and coral reefs would be recognized as “legal persons” with legal rights; high school robotics could become an interscholastic sport; military live-fire training would be banned on state land; and a new fee would be charged on any “sugar-sweetened” beverages under new House and Senate bills to be considered during the legislative session that’s scheduled to adjourn May 8.

item.title: Emergency closure scheduled for Kawaihau Road
item.description: KAPAA — The Department of Public Works is announcing emergency lane closures and intermittent road closures along a portion of Kawaihau Road between Nunu Road and Mailihuna Road, in the vicinity of Kapaa Elementary School on Feb. 6, from 8 a.m. to 12 p.m., weather permitting.
